must: Cloud = shared resources over the Internet, **on demand, pay per use** — like the **electricity grid**.
5 characteristics: **on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service**.
**IaaS** (you manage app, data, OS — e.g. EC2), **PaaS** (only your app — App Engine, Azure), **SaaS** (nothing — Gmail, Salesforce).
Deployment: **public, private (on-premise / externally hosted), community, hybrid**.
Enabling technologies: grid, cluster, utility computing, **virtualization** (key), SOA.
Economics: **CapEx → OpEx**; billed by utility or subscription. Not always cheaper for steady 24/7 loads.
Challenges: data control, replication, latency, unsupported apps, **vendor lock-in**; providers: SLA compliance, licensing, proprietary APIs.
formulas: Charges: instances, data transfer in/out, storage (GB-month), I/O & PUT/GET requests, IPs, load balancing
traps: Saying cloud is always cheaper — steady long-term workloads can cost more to rent.
Putting databases under the consumer in PaaS — in PaaS the provider manages DB/OS.
'Discuss security' with only one side — give **better** (expert teams) **and worse** (loss of control, audits).
likely: Recommend a deployment model for a scenario (hospital → hybrid; shared regulation → community).
Explain how Amazon's ~10% utilisation led to AWS (2006).
tricks: Pizza: home-made = on-prem, rented kitchen = IaaS, take-and-bake = PaaS, dine-in = SaaS.
